blocks.text: About this course: all PDFs teach the Dutch of the Netherlands. About 6 million people in Flanders (Belgium) also speak Dutch. The grammar and spelling are the same, but some words, the pronunciation and the style are different. This PDF helps you understand Flemish speakers; you don't need to copy them.

blocks.title: schoon: clean or beautiful?
blocks.text: In the Netherlands schoon means clean. In Flanders it often means beautiful: Wat een schoon huis! = What a beautiful house! A Fleming who says your house is schoon is paying you a compliment, not inspecting it.

In everyday Flemish, ge / gij is used instead of je / jij, with the verb ending in -t: Gij zijt (jij bent), Hebt ge tijd? (Heb je tijd?), Komt ge mee? Your possessive je / jouw becomes uw. In formal Flemish and in writing, u is used much more than in the Netherlands.

blocks.title: Which accent should you learn?
blocks.text: Learn one, preferably the one of the people around you, and learn to understand the other. Both are correct standard Dutch. Many learners find the Flemish soft g easier to pronounce, and that is perfectly fine in the Netherlands too.

The Dutch are known for their directness: they say what they think, quickly switch to je, and see this as honesty. Flemish speakers are often more formal and indirect: they use u longer, and they soften criticism. Neither is rude; they are different habits.
